title: ReMaP: Macro Placement by Recursively Prototyping and Periphery-Guided Relocating
problem: Macro placement in chip floorplanning directly impacts timing (WNS/TNS) and dataflow efficiency, but expert-quality placement is time-consuming to generate. Existing macro placers lack structured approaches to place macros near periphery while optimizing dataflow and avoiding overlaps.
motivation: Chip design closure requires rapid macro placement tuning; expert practitioners place memory macros and arithmetic blocks peripherally to minimize wire lengths and global routing congestion.
method: ReMaP uses a two-phase approach: ABPlace (angle-based analytical method) arranges macros along an ellipse capturing both dataflow optimization and overlap avoidance, producing rough periphery-aligned distributions. Follow-up heuristic positions macros along chip boundaries, mimicking expert practice. Recursive refinement improves placement quality iteratively. Parameter autotuning via search optimizes tool knobs.
key_novelty: Angle-based analytical placement (ABPlace) combined with periphery-guided relocation, recursively applied to match expert macro placement practices.
contributions: ABPlace angle-based analytical placement optimizing dataflow and overlap
Periphery-guided macro relocation heuristic matching expert practices
Recursive prototyping and refinement for iterative quality improvement
34.15% WNS improvement and 65.39% TNS improvement on OpenROAD benchmarks; 8.75% additional improvement via autotuning

metrics.speedup: 34.15% WNS improvement, 65.39% TNS improvement, 8.75% from autotuning

limitations: Scalability to 5nm+ designs with thousands of macros and applicability to heterogeneous chiplet designs not discussed.
primary_theme: expert-mimicking macro placement via angle-based analytics and periphery-guided relocation
